name: NexusQL Engine
problem: Single-node relational databases often bottleneck on locking contention and lack a custom-built, cost-based query optimizer and vectorized execution pipeline built entirely from scratch.
pain: Standard database internals are buried behind massive legacy codebases, making it difficult to study or experiment with custom cost-based optimizers and lock-free execution engines.
solution: A zero-dependency relational database storage and execution engine written in Java 21 featuring a custom SQL parser, a cost-based optimizer using catalog histograms, a lock-free page cache, and a vectorized Volcano-style iterator model.
verification: Deterministic integration suite executing malformed SQL statements, synthetic out-of-order transaction histories, concurrent write stress tests, and corrupted binary page recovery verification.
major_features: Custom SQL lexer and recursive-descent parser producing an explicit Abstract Syntax Tree
Cost-based query optimizer (CBO) translating logical plans using column statistics histograms
Vectorized execution engine processing blocks of tuples to minimize virtual dispatch overhead
Lock-free page cache implementing an eviction policy with atomic handle tracking
Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC) snapshot isolation engine for concurrent readers and writers
Binary slotted-page storage manager supporting variable-length record packing and splitting
Parallel scan orchestrator utilizing Java 21 Virtual Threads for concurrent block retrieval
Deterministic crash-recovery subsystem replaying a binary Write-Ahead Log (WAL) with checkpoint validation
truth_policy: Only validated behavior may be claimed as working.
